extracted.intended_audience: data journalists, journalism students, and newsrooms
extracted.subtask_description: A broad resource hub listing best practices, handbooks, courses, and short guides for producing trustworthy, accessible, and ethical data journalism, including verification, visualization, analysis, and storytelling techniques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humanise data / connect numbers with people
rubrics_metrics.description: How can journalists connect numbers with people?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use in-depth case studies (e.g., NYT, ProPublica, NPR) to humanise data — connect statistics to real people and narratives so numbers resonate with readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solutions storytelling for climate reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Covering climate change through a solutions and data lens
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use solutions storytelling to engage local communities and bring local reporters together to solve the climate crisis; focus on constructive responses rather than only problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop new climate metrics and visualisations
rubrics_metrics.description: New climate metrics for new climate conversations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop multidisciplinary metrics and visualisations to reshape how we interpret the climate crisis and its impact on people's daily lives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use data to give voice to marginalized groups (gender focus)
rubrics_metrics.description: Data gives voice to women on climate change
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek out and analyse data that reveal disproportionate impacts (e.g., women bearing the brunt of climate change); discover and surface under-used datasets to tell these stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting internet shutdowns with data
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting on and during internet shutdowns
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide practical guides and real-world examples showing what data journalists can do to report on government-imposed shutdowns, including techniques for documenting and raising awareness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use data to amplify coverage of climate refugees
rubrics_metrics.description: Data drives media coverage of climate refugees
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use data journalism techniques and examples from established outlets to give voice to previously overlooked climate refugees and frame their stories with evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility of data visualisations
rubrics_metrics.description: How to create data visualisations that serve the public
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make visualisations accessible to readers with visual impairments and to the general public — include tips to improve accessibility and public-serving design choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextualise data (data are never neutral)
rubrics_metrics.description: Putting data back into context
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognise that data are situated — understand why and how data were collected, their limitations, and the context needed to interpret them responsibly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow (and know when to break) visualization conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: The unspoken rules of visualisation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to fundamental rules and conventions in visualisation for clarity and trustworthiness, but understand the rationale so you can judiciously break rules when justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Go beyond headline metrics in public-health coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting beyond the case numbers: brainstorm COVID-19 data story ideas
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Move past daily infection and death counts to find stories that show the wider impact of health crises on people’s lives; brainstorm diverse data-driven angles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be cautious with news maps and projection choices
rubrics_metrics.description: The essential lies in news maps
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognise that maps distort reality; understand commonly used map types and how to avoid misleading readers through inappropriate projections or representations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design visualisations with empathy
rubrics_metrics.description: Designing data visualisations with empathy
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply empathic approaches in design so audiences (and journalists) can better understand and relate to the subjects represented — use recommended techniques to achieve empathy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice solutions-focused reporting with data
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence of a solution: using data to report more than just bad news
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt solutions journalism frameworks to report responses and evidence of solutions, not only problems; emphasise constructive reporting backed by data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explore new technologies (e.g., blockchain) as data sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Data journalism on the blockchain
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider blockchain both for issues of trust/sustainability and as a source of new data — evaluate the opportunities and limitations for reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embrace spreadsheet and quantitative skills
rubrics_metrics.description: Spreadsheets for journalism
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists should overcome math aversion and learn spreadsheets and functions to work confidently with data; practical overview for beginners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify digital content and UGC (verification practices)
rubrics_metrics.description: Verification Handbook 1 — verifying digital content for emergency coverage
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow established verification steps for user-generated content and digital media during emergencies to ensure accuracy; this edition laid foundations for best practices in verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use online search and open-source research techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: Verification Handbook 2 — online search and research techniques for using UGC and open source information in investigations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply step-by-step online investigation tactics, search methods, and open-source techniques to corroborate information and produce comprehensive investigative reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counter disinformation and media manipulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Verification Handbook 3 — for disinformation and media manipulation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equip journalists with methods to investigate social media accounts, bots, private messaging apps, information operations, deepfakes and other forms of manipulation; use tools and processes for rigorous vetting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand what data journalism is and its limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The Data Journalism Handbook — what is data journalism and what might it do?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reflect on the purposes, opportunities, limitations, and social/political contexts of data journalism; consider who is involved in making and interpreting data-driven work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combine digital-scale data with journalistic judgement
rubrics_metrics.description: How journalists can use data to improve the news
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage the scale and range of digital information together with a journalist’s nose for news to tell compelling stories; use data as either the source or a storytelling tool.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acquire OSINT skills for environmental and investigative reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: OSINT for environmental investigations and open source intelligence techniques
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use open-source intelligence methods to uncover environmental wrongdoing and conduct investigative stories — apply expert insights and practical methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach AI and algorithmic accountability in investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: How to approach AI for investigative reporting
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply algorithmic auditing and accountability principles when investigating AI systems; follow takeaways for responsible coverage and auditing of algorithms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use audience engagement strategies for climate reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Ways to engage audiences with your climate reporting
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ visualisation and storytelling techniques to improve audience engagement for climate coverage and overcome apathy — use recommended tactics from podcast/keynotes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build practitioner skills via short courses (search, coding, Python)
rubrics_metrics.description: Courses: Fundamental search for journalists; Python for journalists; coding
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest in targeted training (search fundamentals, Python, coding) to build practical skills needed for modern data journalism workflows.
